adverse_media.status: Probe into Brazilian subsidiary closed December 2022; CADE scrutiny resumed/ratified October 2023 (no sanction reported)
adverse_media.summary: Brazil's antitrust authority CADE opened a preliminary probe in 2021 into the Brazilian subsidiary of Adyen following a complaint by bank Safra and SafraPay Credenciadora alleging Adyen refused to contract with small payment acquirers; the probe was closed in December 2022, and further scrutiny was ratified in October 2023. Concerns Adyen Do Brasil, a subsidiary, not Adyen N.V. itself.

adverse_media.status: Dismissed - Judge Rita F. Lin (N.D. Cal.) found the allegations conclusory and granted dismissal of the second amended complaint as to the merchant defendant
adverse_media.summary: Smith v. Yeti Coolers LLC (N.D. Cal., No. 3:24-cv-01703): proposed class action alleging Yeti shared its customers' personal and financial information with its third-party payment processor Adyen, allowing Adyen to use the data without consent for Adyen's fraud prevention system. The court dismissed the suit against Yeti on 14 March 2025, calling the allegations that Yeti knew of the processor's conduct conclusory. Names Adyen's fraud-prevention data practices; Adyen was not the dismissed party in this order.

adverse_media.status: Final first-instance judgment, awarding repayment to Adyen (uitvoerbaar bij voorraad)
adverse_media.summary: Rechtbank Amsterdam (ECLI:NL:RBAMS:2024:3288): Adyen, an online payment services provider, was the victim of SEPA direct-debit fraud via defendants' accounts on the Moneybird platform - over 16,000 fraudulent direct-debit orders totalling about EUR 8 million submitted within roughly 1.5 weeks; Adyen had advanced more than EUR 2.6 million and claimed it back. The court ordered the defendants to repay the amounts received plus statutory interest from 2 February 2023. Adyen was the defrauded party, not the wrongdoer.

output.risk_rationale: Low risk. The screened entity is Adyen N.V. (KvK 34259528, LEI 724500973ODKK3IFQ447), an active Dutch naamloze vennootschap seated in Amsterdam, supervised by DNB as a licensed bank ('Bank - CI'). Sanctions screening of the entity returned no true matches: OFAC SDN lists only a namesake Panamanian crude-oil tanker 'AYDEN' (IMO 9365764, IRAN-EO13902), which is not the same party; the EU consolidated list search for 'adyen' returned an empty result set; and the full UK Sanctions List contains no occurrence of 'Adyen'. Directors and supervisory board members were also screened against the UK Sanctions List with no matches (only a fuzzy 'Naydenko' hit for CHRO Brooke Nayden — a different person). No politically exposed person was identified among the board or owners; Adyen N.V. is a widely held listed company (Euronext Amsterdam: ADYEN) with no disclosed controlling shareholder. Adverse media over the last 10 years is limited: a Brazilian antitrust probe concerning Adyen's Brazilian subsidiary (opened 2021, closed December 2022, renewed scrutiny ratified October 2023), a US proposed class action over data shared with Adyen's fraud-prevention system in which the co-defendant merchant's dismissal was granted in March 2025, and a May 2024 Amsterdam court judgment in which Adyen recovered over EUR 2.6 million advanced in a SEPA direct-debit fraud it was the victim of. No fines, enforcement orders, money-laundering or corruption allegations against the entity itself were found. This is an assessment based on the cited screening results.
